nodes.label: Conversation answer prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Answers a student's question using only EVIDENCE memories; output is a list of claims each with text and evidence_ids; unsupported claims are discarded. Flagged evidence is unconfirmed and must be disclosed. MODE plan proposes next steps as cited claims.

nodes.label: Change detector prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Classifies a new student statement against existing memories as new, update (with updates_memory_id), or temporary (with valid_to ISO 8601 computed from current date). Prefers new when unsure since a wrong update destroys history; a temporary statement never replaces a permanent memory. Outputs JSON incl. reason.

nodes.label: Intent classification prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Classifies a student message as tell, ask, plan or answer_question. tell fills statement and optional structured subject/attribute/value; answer_question sets memory_id from PENDING QUESTIONS and answer in still_holds|no_longer_holds|corrected with correction and structured. Must not add facts or numbers.

nodes.label: Resume parser prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Extracts candidate profile facts (cgpa, batch, branch, skill, project, preference, availability) with value, verbatim quote and confidence from resume text; student confirms each fact before storage so precision outranks coverage; candidates with non-verbatim quotes are discarded.

nodes.label: JD parser prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Extracts structured opening requirements from a job description: fields with attribute (title, company, role_type, cgpa_cutoff, batch, deadline, location, required_skill, source_url), value, verbatim quote and confidence. Never infers missing values; fields whose quote is not verbatim in the JD are discarded.

nodes.label: Resolver / Curator prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Given a TRIGGER fact change, one derived BELIEF and its CURRENT PARENTS, decides action keep|update|retire|ask with new_content, question, evidence_refs and reason. Does not change beliefs that are still correct; never invents facts.

nodes.label: Dependency linker prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Given one NEW memory and CANDIDATE memories, proposes dependency links: candidate_id, candidate_is (parent|dependent), link_type from allowed types in message, confidence, reason. A link means if the parent changed the dependent could become wrong. No link is better than a wrong link.

nodes.label: Resume tailoring prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Selects which of the student's real projects and skills (candidate memories) to highlight for one job opening; each highlight has memory_id, reason and opening_evidence_ids; ids outside the candidates are discarded; prefers fewer, stronger highlights; flagged candidates may be highlighted with the marker.

nodes.label: ADR-0020: Change detection: deterministic for structured facts, LLM for prose
nodes.norm_label: adr-0020: change detection: deterministic for structured facts, llm for prose
nodes.rationale: FR-5 needs to detect new/replace/temporary; an LLM call per statement is expensive and non-deterministic where mechanical. Intake classifies in two stages: deterministic structured subject+attribute match is an update; LLM (change_detector.v1) for prose returns new|update(id)|temporary(valid_to) via validated schema given current date. Prompt prefers 'new' when unsure because wrong update rewrites history.

nodes.label: ADR-0030: An opening is one anchor memory plus one structured fact per field
nodes.community_name: ADR-0030: An opening is one anchor memory plus one structured fact per field
nodes.norm_label: adr-0030: an opening is one anchor memory plus one structured fact per field
nodes.rationale: Ripple engine propagates only along links between memories and rules only read StructuredFact triples. One memory per JD would make a deadline change an LLM-interpreted prose edit; fields without grouping can't be forgotten as a unit. record_opening writes one anchor memory (kind opening) plus a field fact per parsed field linked field--depends_on_fact-->anchor, all in one transaction with one ChangeEvent; OpeningFieldRule keeps/retires fields deterministically; stable opening_key survives versioning; one live opening per source.
nodes.revisit_if: Scout re-fetches openings often enough that diffing fields into updates becomes the main write path
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected: one memory per JD with dict structured; N+1 ChangeEvents per JD (not atomic, noisy); anchor depends on fields (orphans on forget); no ChangeEvent at all (inconsistent). Cost: one deterministic keep wave per JD; multi-valued required_skill facts conflict with Intake same-subject+attribute update rule (raised as contract question).

nodes.label: Stale-action window metric
nodes.rationale: Events during which a recommendation was shown that gold says was stale, summed per scenario. Additive to rate-per-event metrics; LLM judge on transcripts kept only as secondary check.

nodes.label: Active learning from pilot corrections
nodes.rationale: Pilot corrections enter training with uncertainty sampling: pairs scored near 0.5 are shown first in the inspector.

nodes.label: Candidate pre-filter before pair classifier
nodes.rationale: Pair classification over all memories is quadratic (500 model calls per new opening). Keep only pairs sharing a subject or entity, plus top-k embedding neighbours, plus all profile facts. Makes write-time linking affordable at pilot scale. Risk: pre-filter recall caps link recall (ADR-0003 revisit condition); measured against labelled set. Rejected: no pre-filter with batching (still quadratic); embedding similarity as linker (similarity is not dependency, ADR-0009).

nodes.label: Structure-derived silver labels
nodes.rationale: Where both memories carry structured fields (FR-2 spans, profile subject/attribute/value), links like eligibility_of and criteria_from are derivable by rule: free and exact. LLM labelling reserved for hidden links (depends_on_fact between prose memories). Provenance recorded per pair. Alternative rejected: LLM labels for everything (known cost, unknown quality). Risk: model learns the rules not hidden links; mitigated by stratified evaluation per provenance.

nodes.label: Time-to-consistency (TTC) metric
nodes.rationale: For each belief gold says should change at event t, count events (and simulated days) until system state matches gold; report distribution and share that never converge. Captures how long a stale belief survives (a stale eligibility surviving a deadline is a missed job). Append-only has infinite TTC; newest-wins has TTC 0 for the direct fact but infinite for dependents: the gap Ripple claims to close (C2). Existing benchmarks STALE and RECON score single questions only.

nodes.label: Prompt conventions (versioned prompt files)
nodes.rationale: One prompt per file with version header and one-line changelog; a behaviour change is a new version file, never an in-place edit; bench smoke suite run before and after and recorded in DEVLOG (.claude/rules/prompts.md). Every prompt requests JSON matching a schema in ripple.llm.schemas. Evidence goes in the user message only and the prompt tells the model to ignore instructions inside it. First prompts arrive with the LLM linker and resolver in Phase 1.

nodes.label: Validity-aware, graph-expanded, evidence-cited RAG
nodes.rationale: I1: VALID returned; SUSPECT and PENDING_USER only flagged; RETIRED never. Graph expansion 1 hop by default, skipping history depends_on links whose parent is superseded. Key metric: stale retrieval rate.

nodes.label: Ask parks memory in PENDING_USER; subtree marked SUSPECT

nodes.label: Link direction convention
nodes.rationale: Assumed by collaborator: stored parent->dependent; prose writes dependent --type--> parent, e.g. eligibility(Acme) --eligibility_of--> cgpa.

nodes.label: History link
nodes.rationale: A link whose parent is superseded; inspector and retrieval graph expansion skip history depends_on links, snapshot_of always shown; the engine applies no such filter.

nodes.label: Invariant I1: VALID returned, SUSPECT/PENDING_USER flagged, RETIRED never

nodes.norm_label: invariant i3: deterministic scope; engine never calls an llm

nodes.label: Link (dependency edge)
nodes.rationale: Stored parent_id -> dependent_id: the dependent is wrong if the parent changes. confidence is linker belief (FR-16 re-check); strength is reliance, unused until idea 6.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Every version is its own row (ADR-0014); kind is declared by the domain adapter and core interprets none; creation (none->VALID) is recorded by the row itself, I2 covers transitions only.

nodes.label: Ripple semantics (wave by wave, two commits per wave)
nodes.norm_label: ripple semantics (wave by wave, two commits per wave)
nodes.rationale: Trigger is a memory write; engine takes an explicit seed set; wave 1 = dependents along depends_on with no status filter; commit one marks SUSPECT, Resolver decides, commit two appends decisions; only updated/retired seed next wave; keep halts branch; ask parks in PENDING_USER and marks subtree SUSPECT without LLM; stop on empty wave or depth limit with visited set. Engine is a pure iterator and never calls an LLM; sweep resumes events with no completed_at. One transaction per ripple is impossible once a wave waits on a user.

nodes.label: Seed set
nodes.rationale: Explicit seed set (new version for write, retired memory for expiry/retire) is why copying links to new versions works with no status filter.

nodes.label: Temporary fact (valid_to)
nodes.rationale: Temporariness is just an ordinary memory with valid_to filled by the change detector; nothing else marks it (ADR-0015).

nodes.label: Validity states VALID / SUSPECT / RETIRED / PENDING_USER
nodes.norm_label: validity states valid / suspect / retired / pending_user
nodes.rationale: Transition table: none->VALID on write; VALID->SUSPECT in wave or below PENDING_USER; SUSPECT->VALID on keep or still-holds; to RETIRED on retire/expiry/new version; any->deleted only via forget API.

nodes.label: Version chain (supersedes_id)
nodes.rationale: Update writes a new row with supersedes_id and retires the old; the chain is supersedes_id only, no supersedes link.

nodes.label: Wave (set of dependents resolved together)
nodes.rationale: Each wave is two commits; decisions tagged with wave number; wave 0 = deterministic restoration recorded by an answer.

nodes.label: Worked example: cgpa 7.6 -> 7.9 ripple
nodes.rationale: cgpa v2 supersedes v1; incoming links copied; wave 1 = eligibility(Acme) and criteria -> update; wave 2 recommendation; wave 3 empty; Scout re-runs because criteria changed. One ChangeEvent holds all decisions.

nodes.label: Worked example: busy-with-exams expiry
nodes.rationale: Fact with valid_to ripples normally; sweep retires it on expiry (trigger_kind=expiry) with the retired fact as seed set; wave 1 = availability restored; no LLM needed to detect expiry.

nodes.label: Ablations
nodes.rationale: Without graph; LLM linker instead of trained; without Curator; without evidence retrieval; without ask-user.

nodes.label: Decision: graph decides scope, LLM decides action
nodes.norm_label: decision: graph decides scope, llm decides action
nodes.rationale: Check-everything costs one LLM call per memory per change and LLM-chosen scope is non-deterministic and untestable. Embedding-similarity scoping misses non-textual dependents (CGPA to eligibility). Quality is bounded by link recall, so missed-link rate is measured. Revisit if link recall stays below target after Phase 4.

nodes.label: Ripple flow (wave by wave)
nodes.rationale: A memory write is the trigger; engine takes the seed set and emits wave 1 = dependents along depends_on with no status filter and no LLM; they become SUSPECT and commit; Resolver decides keep/update/retire/ask; only updated/retired seed the next wave; keep halts the branch; ask parks in PENDING_USER; repeat until empty wave or depth limit; sweep resumes ripples with no completed_at.

nodes.label: Write flow (ripple.core.intake)

nodes.label: Open architecture decisions (identity/auth, embedding, checkpointer, resume parser)
nodes.norm_label: open architecture decisions (identity/auth, embedding, checkpointer, resume parser)

nodes.label: Security: untrusted retrieved text, allowed-sources registry, secrets in env
nodes.norm_label: security: untrusted retrieved text, allowed-sources registry, secrets in env
nodes.rationale: Retrieved text is untrusted: evidence only in user messages with injection defence in prompts; allowed-sources registry for Scout (ADR-0008); secrets only in env, never logged.

nodes.label: Decision: PostgreSQL + pgvector with in-process graph traversal
nodes.norm_label: decision: postgresql + pgvector with in-process graph traversal
nodes.rationale: Needs relational data, vectors and transactional commits in one store; per-user graphs are small so Python traversal suffices. Rejected: Neo4j (extra service), Qdrant+Postgres (two stores to keep consistent), SQLite (weak concurrency/vector support). One backup/migration story; ripple commits atomic. Revisit if a user graph exceeds ~100k memories.

nodes.label: Decision: LangGraph for agents, core stays framework-free
nodes.norm_label: decision: langgraph for agents, core stays framework-free
nodes.rationale: Agents need durable state, retries, human-in-the-loop pauses and background runs; hand-rolled loops would reinvent checkpointing. src/ripple/core never imports LangGraph; framework churn contained to src/ripple/agents.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: Retire, never silently delete
nodes.rationale: Explanations, undo and auditing need history; privacy needs real deletion. State changes keep history via ChangeEvents; hard deletion only through the forget API.
nodes.revisit_if: Storage cost becomes a problem in the pilot
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected overwrite in place (no history/undo/explanations) and soft-delete flag only (no reasons, not real deletion). Cost: storage grows, needs retention policy; forget must truly delete per DPDP Act.

nodes.label: ADR-0013: Wave-by-wave ripple over core link classes
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013: wave-by-wave ripple over core link classes
nodes.rationale: Graph decides scope, LLM decides action; need chains of 3+ hops and a link class that never propagates. Engine emits waves along depends_on links; each wave commits as one transaction; keep halts a branch; ask parks memory in PENDING_USER and marks subtree SUSPECT; two link classes (depends_on, snapshot_of) in core; engine never calls an LLM (I3). Decided in kickoff interview; transaction boundary and two-class reduction from architecture-guardian review.
nodes.revisit_if: RippleBench chain scenarios show closure-first catches dependents the wave approach misses, or a domain needs behaviour neither class expresses
nodes.status: Accepted (approved by author same day); amends ADR-0003, ADR-0004, wording of ADR-0007/I7
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected full transitive closure first (more LLM cost and over-correction), one transaction per ripple (impossible with LLM/user waits; hides SUSPECT from retrieval), per-link-type policy registry (testability), separate depends_on/derived_from classes, fixed generic types only (loses typed signal for link finder). Cost: latency grows with chain depth; wrong keep stops propagation; whole subtree SUSPECT while ask pending; crash leaves open ChangeEvent resumed by nightly sweep.

nodes.label: ADR-0014: Memory versions are rows; dependency links are copied to the new version
nodes.norm_label: adr-0014: memory versions are rows; dependency links are copied to the new version
nodes.rationale: Without copying, dependents' links point at the old row and the graph dies after one ripple. Every version is its own Memory row with supersedes_id; update in one transaction writes new row, retires old, copies incoming and outgoing depends_on links (outgoing re-pointed at parents' latest), leaves snapshot_of on the old row. History links (parent superseded) are skipped by inspector and retrieval expansion. From kickoff interview and architecture-guardian review.
nodes.revisit_if: Link-copy bugs appear in pilot or update latency exceeds NFR; then supersede with stable-identity design
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected stable identity with history table (author prefers one table; copy rule gives snapshot semantics free), move/re-point (loses history), leaving outgoing links to Linker only (one missed link detaches version), overwrite in place. Cost: every update is a graph rewrite that must be transactional (NFR-4); link rows grow; in-memory and Postgres stores must share the filter.

nodes.label: ADR-0015: Every change is a memory write; temporary facts self-expire
nodes.norm_label: adr-0015: every change is a memory write; temporary facts self-expire
nodes.rationale: Data model lacked an entity for ripple trigger and a place to store temporariness (FR-5). Trigger of every ripple is a memory write (new, new version incl. user edit, or expiry); temporary fact is an ordinary memory with valid_to; ChangeEvent gains trigger_kind; retrieval treats PENDING_USER like SUSPECT. Points 1-2 decided in kickoff; 3-4 are collaborator's recommended option, open to reversal.
nodes.revisit_if: Author answers question 5 differently (supersede points 3-4), or expiry ripples prove noisy because detector fills valid_to badly
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected separate ChangeRequest entity, polymorphic ChangeEvent.trigger, classifying temporary only in detector without valid_to. Cost: FakeClock scenario for FR-5; one I2 invariant test per trigger kind; sweep needs index on valid_to.

nodes.label: ChangeEvent
nodes.rationale: One per ripple, created in the trigger write transaction and appended per wave; trigger_kind in ripple|expiry|user_edit|user_answer; completed_at null while open lets the sweep find ripples to resume; makes I2 testable per trigger kind (ADR-0015).

nodes.label: ForgetEvent
nodes.rationale: Forget is deletion, not a state change, so it has no ChangeEvent (I7).

nodes.label: Invariant I7: forget deletes whole version chain and cascades
nodes.norm_label: invariant i7: forget deletes whole version chain and cascades
nodes.rationale: Forget applies to a whole version chain and cascades along depends_on links whose parent is in the chain; ADR-0007 calls this cascading along derived_from links.

nodes.label: Link type registry: depends_on_fact, depends_on_time_period, eligibility_of, fit_of, reminder_for, criteria_from, sent_with_resume
nodes.norm_label: link type registry: depends_on_fact, depends_on_time_period, eligibility_of, fit_of, reminder_for, criteria_from, sent_with_resume
nodes.rationale: sent_with_resume is snapshot_of so a new resume never ripples into past applications; all others are depends_on. Provenance to sources is source_ref, not a link, because sources are not memories.

nodes.label: Link class: depends_on
nodes.rationale: Propagates a change; copied to new version on update; on forget of parent the dependent is hard-deleted (cascade).

nodes.label: Link class: snapshot_of
nodes.rationale: Does not propagate; not copied to the new version; on forget of parent the link is removed and dependent kept. Makes the correct non-update case for sent applications fall out of the copy rule.

nodes.label: Link classes (core) vs link types (domains)
nodes.rationale: Core knows two classes with fixed behaviour; each domain link type maps to exactly one; the registry lives in the domain adapter and is applied in the write flow, never in core.

nodes.label: Versioning: copy incoming and outgoing depends_on links to the new version
nodes.norm_label: versioning: copy incoming and outgoing depends_on links to the new version
nodes.rationale: Incoming links copied so the new version has same dependents (retired dependents not copied; one per dependent,type); outgoing links copied re-pointed at each parent latest version so later parent changes still reach the new version even if the Linker misses; snapshot_of stays on old row; crash rolls back everything (ADR-0014).

nodes.tradeoffs: Lease stops sweep-vs-sweep but not sweep-vs-slow-live-ripple; InMemoryDeliveryLog forgets on restart; global lease and per-event runner lease deferred.

nodes.norm_label: jobs_rules() ruleresolver chain (field, eligibility, fit, reminder, criteria)
nodes.rationale: One rule per belief kind (EligibilityRule, FitRule, ReminderRule, CriteriaRule, OpeningFieldRule) with disjoint kinds; returns None when parents in doubt, retire when anchor retired, keep when recomputation equals stored, else update with evidence_refs.

nodes.label: Deterministic rule links for facts recorded later (fit_of, criteria_from)
nodes.norm_label: deterministic rule links for facts recorded later (fit_of, criteria_from)
nodes.rationale: A belief links only to parents it read when derived, so profile.record_profile_fact writes fit_of and criteria_from links for later skills, cgpa and batch.

nodes.label: JobsRecommender (RecommendationSource implementation)
nodes.rationale: Reads only memories via visible_for_retrieval with include_flagged=True; SUSPECT/PENDING_USER set flagged=True; now is injected so ranking is deterministic and offline-testable.

nodes.label: Tier ordering and company-variety rebuild
nodes.rationale: Eligible, then deadline within 48h, then higher fit, then earlier deadline; within each tier greedy selection of least-seen company.

nodes.label: STATUS_FOR exception-to-HTTP table
nodes.rationale: Single table: not found 404, NotPendingError 409, unparseable 422, LLM failures 503.

nodes.label: Services frozen dataclass
nodes.rationale: Holds store, clock, link registry, Intake, RippleRunner, UserStore, CandidateStore, EventLog and injected contracts.

nodes.label: POST /memories/{id}/edit as user_edit via update_memory
nodes.rationale: Uses TriggerKind.USER_EDIT, created_by user, bypasses Intake; PENDING_USER edit is 409 pointing to answer endpoint.

nodes.label: Known erasure gap: ChangeEvents survive DELETE /me
nodes.norm_label: known erasure gap: changeevents survive delete /me
nodes.rationale: Core forget removes memories and links only; ChangeEvent decision reasons may quote content until Store offers per-user event deletion.

nodes.label: Declared Capability set checked for I6
nodes.norm_label: declared capability set checked for i6
nodes.rationale: Agent exposes closed Capability set; test checks allowlist and scans imports for network reach.

nodes.label: AnswerVerdict claims with evidence_ids filtering
nodes.rationale: Claims kept only if an evidence id was retrieved this turn; flagged evidence rendered (unconfirmed) by code; zero hits gives no-model reply.

nodes.label: Numeric grounding of tell restatements
nodes.rationale: If restatement contains a number absent from the message, the student's message is recorded as prose (I5).

nodes.label: TailorVerdict highlights filtered to candidate ids
nodes.norm_label: tailorverdict highlights filtered to candidate ids
nodes.rationale: Highlights with unknown or repeated memory ids dropped and counted; no candidates means no model call.

nodes.label: One-hop graph expansion with visibility-aware seeds
nodes.norm_label: one-hop graph expansion with visibility-aware seeds
nodes.rationale: Both link directions from visible hits; skips superseded depends_on, follows snapshot_of; neighbours score half and carry via=GRAPH evidence.

nodes.label: append_only and newest_wins baselines
nodes.rationale: No propagation; append_only restores superseded version as wave-0 KEEP decision (I2).

nodes.label: check_everything baseline (one-shot all-VALID wave)
nodes.rationale: Accuracy ceiling at cost ceiling, the H1 reference; ignores the graph but keeps Ripple commit protocol.

nodes.label: manifest.json persona/template split with sha256
nodes.rationale: train = train persona and train template; strict_test = both unseen; --check verifies checked-in data equals fresh generation.

nodes.label: Seven gold-behaviour template families
nodes.rationale: cgpa_rise, deadline_moved, exam_block, accepted_offer, cutoff_unknown, resume_update, forget_cgpa; 35 scenarios and 175 gold checks.

nodes.label: StubActionLayer placeholder for RecommendationSource
nodes.rationale: ActionLayer is the bench name for contract C1; stub recommends VALID openings unless eligibility dependent starts with 'not '; applied identically to all strategies.

nodes.label: stale_retrieval_rate and stale_recommendation_rate
nodes.rationale: Unflagged results resting on gold-stale beliefs; flagged results count as warned (I1).

nodes.label: time_to_consistency metric
nodes.rationale: Events and simulated days until observed satisfies gold; None if new gold arrives first or trace ends.

nodes.label: correct_updates, stale_kept, wrongful_changes
nodes.rationale: Defined from before/observed state vs gold per event; over-correction is should-stay and moved.

nodes.label: LangGraph checkpoints (memory_saver, postgres_saver, six-turn _recent reducer)
nodes.rationale: Thread state keeps only last six turns because the checkpoint copies user text outside the forget API.

nodes.label: _compose_answer claim filtering
nodes.rationale: Prompt asks for citations; code guarantees I5 by keeping only claims with retrieved evidence ids.

nodes.label: I6 route allowlist test (no apply endpoint)
nodes.norm_label: i6 route allowlist test (no apply endpoint)

nodes.label: AliasResolver trigger-scoped scripted oracle
nodes.rationale: Scripted oracle measures engine and write semantics at zero LLM cost; trigger scoping prevents check_everything applying every gold decision.

nodes.label: Worked metrics example (3 correct, 1 stale kept, 1 wrongful, accuracy 3/4)
nodes.norm_label: worked metrics example (3 correct, 1 stale kept, 1 wrongful, accuracy 3/4)
nodes.rationale: Hand computation pinning metric definitions; mirrored by xfail-strict tests in tests/scenarios/test_bench_metrics.py.

nodes.label: Invariant I1: retrieval never returns RETIRED, flags SUSPECT/PENDING_USER
nodes.norm_label: invariant i1: retrieval never returns retired, flags suspect/pending_user

nodes.label: Invariant I5: agent never invents facts or numbers
nodes.norm_label: invariant i5: agent never invents facts or numbers

nodes.label: Invariant I6: no acting on external sites
nodes.norm_label: invariant i6: no acting on external sites

nodes.label: Invariant I7: hard deletion only through the forget API
nodes.norm_label: invariant i7: hard deletion only through the forget api

nodes.label: ADR index (README)
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADRs are never edited, only superseded; workstream ADR ranges WS-1 0030-0034 through WS-8 0065-0069.

nodes.label: Learning page: ripple.agents Conversation and Tailor
nodes.norm_label: learning page: ripple.agents conversation and tailor

nodes.label: Learning page: bench strategies, generator, replay harness, metrics
nodes.norm_label: learning page: bench strategies, generator, replay harness, metrics

nodes.label: ADR-0031 Jobs rule resolvers recompute derived beliefs from parents
nodes.norm_label: adr-0031 jobs rule resolvers recompute derived beliefs from parents
nodes.rationale: Derived beliefs (eligibility, fit, reminder, criteria) are arithmetic over structured fields so bench claim C4 needs them to never require a model call; content and structured value are pure functions of parents.
nodes.tradeoffs: A wrong rule is confidently wrong; content formats become a contract between derivation and rules; eligibility asymmetry (no cutoff = eligible, no CGPA = no belief).

nodes.label: ADR-0032 Ranking openings: eligible, urgent, fit, variety; flagged never retired
nodes.norm_label: adr-0032 ranking openings: eligible, urgent, fit, variety; flagged never retired
nodes.rationale: Ranking must come from memory-layer beliefs, not JD recomputation, otherwise stale beliefs are invisible to the layer that flags them (I1, C2). Tiers are explainable to students unlike a weighted score.
nodes.tradeoffs: Fit-before-urgency and weighted score rejected; past-deadline openings vanish from list but stay in memory; missing CGPA ranks cutoff openings as not eligible.

nodes.label: ADR-0040 Identity: admin-created users, hashed bearer tokens, Telegram link codes
nodes.norm_label: adr-0040 identity: admin-created users, hashed bearer tokens, telegram link codes
nodes.rationale: Pilot is 10-15 hand-enrolled students; every call must be user-scoped; sha256-only token storage means a DB dump grants no access; 404 not 403 avoids confirming ids across tenants.
nodes.tradeoffs: One admin step per student; tokens never expire; OAuth, clear API keys and JWTs rejected.

nodes.label: ADR-0041 API composition: create_app(services), Services, environment-only wiring
nodes.norm_label: adr-0041 api composition: create_app(services), services, environment-only wiring
nodes.rationale: Tests must run offline and settings must never live in code; app state read from request.app.state so two apps share nothing; protocols let API build without sibling workstreams.
nodes.tradeoffs: Depends-with-singletons, pydantic-settings and direct WS-1/WS-2 imports rejected; EventLog duplicates Store queries as stop-gap.

nodes.label: ADR-0042 Inspector endpoints: I1 at boundary, history on request, edits straight to versioning
nodes.norm_label: adr-0042 inspector endpoints: i1 at boundary, history on request, edits straight to versioning
nodes.rationale: FR-12 inspector; edit named by the user so Intake change detection would only guess and an LLM NEW verdict could duplicate prose memories; forget is the only deletion path (I7).
nodes.tradeoffs: Edits skip the Linker so new versions gain no new links; question text not stored so decision reason shown.

nodes.label: ADR-0043 Resume candidates live in their own table until the user decides
nodes.norm_label: adr-0043 resume candidates live in their own table until the user decides
nodes.rationale: FR-1/I5: no fact stored without confirmation; server keeps values so it never trusts the client's resent values; rejected rows kept so user sees what they declined.
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected rows accumulate; retention sweep later.

nodes.label: ADR-0044 Export everything, delete through forget, keep the deletion audit
nodes.norm_label: adr-0044 export everything, delete through forget, keep the deletion audit
nodes.rationale: FR-15/NFR-3 DPDP alignment; deletion goes through forget (I7); ForgetEvents hold no content and prove deletion happened.
nodes.tradeoffs: ChangeEvents remain after DELETE /me so erasure is incomplete (known gap); no soft-delete or grace period.

nodes.label: ADR-0045 Conversation agent: one LangGraph turn, strict intent, evidence-only answers
nodes.norm_label: adr-0045 conversation agent: one langgraph turn, strict intent, evidence-only answers
nodes.rationale: FR-10/FR-7 with I5 (no invention) and I6 (no external action); claim schema makes support structural; agent must reuse Intake and core.answers, not reimplement.
nodes.tradeoffs: True claims with forgotten citations are dropped; misread-but-cited claims not caught; numeric-only grounding; checkpoint is user text outside forget API; prompts jobs-flavoured.

nodes.label: ADR-0046 Tailor agent: read-only, picks from id-validated candidates
nodes.norm_label: adr-0046 tailor agent: read-only, picks from id-validated candidates
nodes.rationale: FR-11 suggest real projects without inventing; model good at matching, bad at being trusted with the project list; docs/02 gives Tailor read-only permission.
nodes.tradeoffs: Suggestions only as complete as candidate set; domain-specific by design; model-written paragraphs and persisted suggestions rejected.

nodes.label: ADR-0060 Baseline memory strategies behind one MemoryStrategy protocol
nodes.norm_label: adr-0060 baseline memory strategies behind one memorystrategy protocol
nodes.rationale: Fair H1 comparison needs same writes, scripted resolver, clock and same cost counting; only propagation should vary.
nodes.tradeoffs: as_runner cast; Mem0-style baseline undecided; real-resolver over-correction is Phase 3.

nodes.label: ADR-0061 RippleBench v0 jobs track generated from seeded personas and templates
nodes.norm_label: adr-0061 ripplebench v0 jobs track generated from seeded personas and templates
nodes.rationale: Hand-written scenarios drift and item-level splits leak into link-finder training; split by persona and template; seeded RNG keeps persona i stable.
nodes.tradeoffs: Data small and regular so v0 measures engine not language; template change changes every persona file; LLM-generated scenarios deferred to v1.

nodes.label: ADR-0062 Time-to-consistency replay harness with per-event snapshots
nodes.norm_label: adr-0062 time-to-consistency replay harness with per-event snapshots
nodes.rationale: Rate metrics do not say how long a stale belief survives; snapshots after every event let TTC and stale-action window be computed, and gold checks read the same snapshot as the metrics.
nodes.tradeoffs: Stub action layer reads content heuristically; snapshots per alias only; larger results/ runs.

nodes.label: ADR-0063 Metric definitions for RippleBench v0
nodes.norm_label: adr-0063 metric definitions for ripplebench v0
nodes.rationale: Exact definitions fixed before any number is published (ADR-0012, I8); bodies are [human] Phase 3 task; counted over gold targets not all memories.
nodes.tradeoffs: Proposed H1 accuracy = correct_updates / should-change targets; changing a definition requires new ADR and rerun; TTC in events/days not seconds.

nodes.label: BM25 in-memory and ts_rank_cd Postgres lexical scoring
nodes.norm_label: bm25 in-memory and ts_rank_cd postgres lexical scoring
nodes.rationale: BM25 k1=1.5 b=0.75 over deterministic tokeniser; Postgres to_tsvector/plainto_tsquery with GIN expression index; TF-IDF rejected for lacking saturation.

nodes.label: ADR-0050 Lexical BM25/FTS, RRF fusion, one-hop graph expansion for retrieval
nodes.norm_label: adr-0050 lexical bm25/fts, rrf fusion, one-hop graph expansion for retrieval
nodes.rationale: Offline and Postgres backends must behave alike; I1 visibility enforced last in retriever, not in backends; follows ADR-0014 over the WS-5 brief (snapshot_of links followed).
nodes.tradeoffs: Postgres lexical path searches content only (parity gap); dense path only exercised by fake embedder; up to 2k rows returned; backends oversample 4k+16.

nodes.label: Hand-written deadline normaliser (dates.normalise_deadline)
nodes.rationale: ISO 8601 with offset from located span; year-less dates dropped; day-first numeric dates; no date library because fuzzy mode guesses years.

nodes.label: Forwarded email envelope stripping (strip_email_envelope)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic removal of headers, quote prefixes, disclaimers and signatures before parsing; spans are offsets into stripped text.

nodes.label: Model quotes, code locates (locate_span)
nodes.rationale: Models count characters badly; a wrong offset is undetectable, a wrong quote is. Unfound quote drops the item, no retry.

nodes.label: Regex cross-checks for cgpa_cutoff and deadline
nodes.norm_label: regex cross-checks for cgpa_cutoff and deadline
nodes.rationale: Second opinion: disagreement caps model field at 0.5, missed value added at 0.6; regexes written not to invent.

nodes.label: ADR-0035 Parsers: LLM extraction with deterministic span, value and date validation
nodes.norm_label: adr-0035 parsers: llm extraction with deterministic span, value and date validation
nodes.rationale: A model can satisfy the schema yet misquote, round numbers or emit unusable dates; FR-2 requires every field link to a source span, I4 schema validation, I5 no invention.
nodes.tradeoffs: Recall traded for precision: misquoted fields, year-less deadlines and out-of-scale numbers are dropped not guessed; confidence 0.5/0.6 are policy constants; 4-point GPA silently accepted.

nodes.label: owned_memory single dereference point (404 across users)
nodes.norm_label: owned_memory single dereference point (404 across users)
nodes.rationale: 404 not 403 hides id existence at cost of less specific error for buggy clients.
